## Research that can be inspected, rerun, and published

This site is a home for reproducible geospatial workflows. Articles are written in Quarto; Nix provides the build tools, Pixi supplies a shared R/Python runtime, and GitHub Actions publishes the result.

<div class="docs-pills"><span>Quarto</span><span>Nix Flakes</span><span>Pixi</span><span>R + Python</span><span>GitHub Pages</span></div>

[Explore the architecture](architecture.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [View the source](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog){.btn .btn-outline-secondary target="_blank"}
:::

## The publishing system at a glance

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "The build runs on GitHub Actions; readers receive a static website."
flowchart LR
    A["Quarto source<br/>.qmd + metadata"] --> B["GitHub<br/>main"]
    B --> C["GitHub Actions<br/>Nix + Pixi"]
    C --> D["Quarto<br/>one site render"]
    D --> E["GitHub Pages<br/>gh-pages"]
    F["Saved _freeze<br/>execution results"] <--> C
    E --> G["Readers<br/>HTML + browser JS"]
```

## Reproducibility, with practical limits

A post can contain narrative, analysis, equations, figures, and interactive components in a single version-controlled `.qmd` file. On publication, computational code may run on the CI worker; the final website itself needs no running Python or R server.

::: {.callout-note}
Build tools are pinned by `flake.lock`. The shared `pixi exec` environment resolves compatible conda-forge packages from specifications, not a committed Pixi lockfile. Data changes outside the Quarto source may require intentional cache invalidation.
:::

For implementation details, see [`_quarto.yml`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/_quarto.yml), [`render-site.py`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/scripts/render-site.py), and [`publish.yml`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml).

:::
